name: KAKEYA TORANPU
description: Kakeya Toranpu (also known as Etori) is a unique and rare trick-taking game native to Kakeya Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It utilizes a standard 52-card deck but introduces a 'Master Card' called the 'Rensho' (usually the Ace of Spades). The game features fixed partnerships and a scoring system based on Go stones, representing a rare survival of localized Japanese card game culture from the Edo period influence.

content.text: Kakeya Toranpu (also known as Etori) is a unique and rare trick-taking game native to Kakeya Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It utilizes a standard 52-card deck but introduces a 'Master Card' called the 'Rensho' (usually the Ace of Spades). The game features fixed partnerships and a scoring system based on Go stones, representing a rare survival of localized Japanese card game culture from the Edo period influence.

Believed to have been introduced to Kakeya Town in the mid-18th century by a localized doctor who returned from Nagasaki (the only port open to Westerners during the Sakoku era). It resembles early Portuguese 'Hombre' or 'Renette' variants.
4 or 6 players. In 6-player games, two players sit out each round as dealers.
Standard 52-card deck. Aces are high, 2s are low.
Standard cards, Go stones for scoring, lottery sticks for partnership selection
Two players (the Kubariban) deal the entire deck. Each active player gets 13 cards.

items.text: Etori: The alternative name used for the game within the town.
Kakeya 6-Player: A specific rotation variant where players cycle between dealer and taker roles.
4-Player Standard: The most common competitive format.
